REQUIREMENT SLUG: hdfsfederationbalance-doc-correction
REQUIREMENT FILE: /workspace/requirements/hdfsfederationbalance-doc-correction.yaml   <-- READ THIS FIRST

The `title:` field names the real upstream Apache Hadoop JIRA / git commit. Your job is to reproduce that upstream change as faithfully as you can from the requirement text plus the code you find in the tree. Hidden tests derived from the real upstream commit will grade the result, so EXACT naming matters:
  * new/changed configuration keys and their default values (and their entries in *-default.xml)
  * new class / interface / method / field / metric names and their visibility
  * log message wording and format placeholders
  * behavioural details (return values, exception types, ordering, off-by-one boundaries)
If the requirement text names an identifier (class, method, config key, metric, constant), use that identifier verbatim.

HOW TO WORK
1. Read the requirement yaml. Note the JIRA id and the module it belongs to (HDFS / YARN / MAPREDUCE / HADOOP-common / tools).
2. Locate the real code with Grep/Glob. Read enough surrounding code (and the existing tests for it) to make a correct, idiomatic change.
3. Implement the change. Match the surrounding code style, license headers, checkstyle habits (2-space indent, 80-col-ish, final where used, LOG placeholders `{}`).
4. If the change adds a config key, also add it to the matching `*-default.xml` (hdfs-default.xml / core-default.xml / yarn-default.xml / mapred-default.xml) with a sensible description, and to the `DFSConfigKeys`/`YarnConfiguration`/etc. constants class the module uses. Some modules have a TestYarnConfigurationFields / TestHdfsConfigFields style test that requires the xml and the constant to agree - keep them in sync.
5. If the upstream change would have come with tests, add or extend the corresponding test class under the same module (src/test/java/...). Keep tests deterministic and cheap. Do not add tests that need network or a real cluster beyond the usual MiniDFSCluster/MiniYARNCluster idioms already used in that test file.
6. Do NOT run maven/mvn or cmake (there is no warm build environment; it wastes your time). Instead be rigorous by inspection: every symbol you reference must exist (grep to confirm), every new import must be needed and correct, braces/parens balanced, no stale references left behind. Re-read your own final diff (`git diff -- <your files>`) before finishing and fix anything sloppy.
7. Scope discipline: change ONLY what this requirement needs. Do not reformat unrelated lines, do not fix unrelated warnings, do not touch other subsystems. Other agents are concurrently implementing ~380 other requirements in this same working tree.

FORBIDDEN COMMANDS (they would destroy other agents' concurrent work): git checkout / switch / stash / reset / revert / clean / rebase / merge / cherry-pick, `git add -A` or `git add .` without an explicit pathspec, `git commit --amend`, `git rm` of files you did not create, and any `mvn`/`gradle` invocation.

WHEN YOUR IMPLEMENTATION IS COMPLETE - commit it yourself with exactly this shape (substitute the real repo-relative paths you touched, space separated, and keep the flock):

  cd /workspace && flock /tmp/hadoop-git.lock bash -c 'git add -A -- PATH1 PATH2 ... && git diff --cached --binary > requirement_patches/hdfsfederationbalance-doc-correction.diff && git commit -q -m "impl: hdfsfederationbalance-doc-correction" && git log --oneline -1 && wc -c requirement_patches/hdfsfederationbalance-doc-correction.diff'

Rules for that step:
  * List every file you created, modified or deleted as an explicit pathspec. Never a bare directory like `.`.
  * requirement_patches/hdfsfederationbalance-doc-correction.diff MUST come out non-empty (wc -c > 0). If `git commit` reports "nothing to commit", another agent already committed your lines: verify the requirement is genuinely satisfied in the working tree, then report that in your notes.
  * Do not touch requirement_patches/ for any other slug.

FINALLY return ONLY a JSON object (this is your return value, not a message to a human):
{"slug":"hdfsfederationbalance-doc-correction","status":"done"|"partial"|"blocked","files":["..."],"committed":true|false,"patch_bytes":<int>,"summary":"<=3 sentences on what you changed","notes":"anything the orchestrator must know (conflicts, follow-ups, uncertainty)"}

3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  Operators using HDFS federation balancing docs depend on the written guidance being accurate, especially when they are following procedural documentation during cluster maintenance. A small documentation error in the FedBalance material can still create confusion in an operational workflow.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  The HDFS Federation Balance documentation should be corrected so the affected guidance reads accurately and consistently. This is a documentation-only fix, so the balancing feature itself and its operational behavior must remain unchanged.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  The incorrect text in the HDFSFederationBalance documentation is corrected, the surrounding guidance reads cleanly for operators following the document, and no runtime behavior or command semantics change.
16	
17	  '

14	
15	HDFS Federation Balance Guide
16	=====================
17	
18	<!-- MACRO{toc|fromDepth=0|toDepth=3} -->
19	
20	Overview
21	--------
22	
23	  HDFS Federation Balance is a tool balancing data across different federation
24	  namespaces. It uses [DistCp](../hadoop-distcp/DistCp.html) to copy data from
25	  the source path to the target path. First it creates a snapshot at the source
26	  path and submits the initial distcp. Second it uses distcp diff to do the
27	  incremental copy until the source and the target are the same. Then If it's
28	  working in RBF mode it updates the mount table in Router. Finally it moves the
29	  source to trash.
30	
31	  This document aims to describe the usage and design of the HDFS Federation
32	  Balance.
33	
34	Usage
35	-----
36	
37	### Basic Usage
38	
39	  The hdfs federation balance tool supports both normal federation cluster and
40	  router-based federation cluster. Taking rbf for example. Supposing we have a
41	  mount entry in Router:
42	
43	    Source       Destination
44	    /foo/src     hdfs://namespace-0/foo/src
45	
46	  The command below runs an hdfs federation balance job. The first parameter is
47	  the mount entry. The second one is the target path which must include the
48	  target cluster.
49	
50	    bash$ /bin/hadoop rbfbalance -router submit /foo/src hdfs://namespace-1/foo/dst
51	
52	  It copies data from hdfs://namespace-0/foo/src to hdfs://namespace-1/foo/dst
53	  incrementally and finally updates the mount entry to:
54	
55	    Source       Destination
56	    /foo/src     hdfs://namespace-1/foo/dst
57	
58	  If the hadoop shell process exits unexpectedly, we can use the command below
59	  to continue the unfinished job:
60	
61	    bash$ /bin/hadoop rbfbalance continue
62	
63	  This will scan the journal to find all the unfinished jobs, recover and
64	  continue to execute them.
65	
66	  If we want to balance in a normal federation cluster, use the command below.
67	
68	    bash$ /bin/hadoop fedbalance submit hdfs://namespace-0/foo/src hdfs://namespace-1/foo/dst
69	
70	  In normal federation mode the source path must includes the path schema.
71	
72	### RBF Mode And Normal Federation Mode
73	
74	  The hdfs federation balance tool has 2 modes:
75	
76	  * the router-based federation mode (RBF mode).
77	  * the normal federation mode.
78	
79	  The command `rbfbalance` runs in router-based federation mode. The command
80	  `fedbalance` runs in normal federation mode.
81	
82	  In the rbf mode the first parameter is taken as the mount point. It disables
83	  write by setting the mount point readonly.
84	
85	  In the normal federation mode the first parameter is taken as the full path of
86	  the source. The first parameter must include the source cluster. It disables
87	  write by cancelling all the permissions of the source path.
88	
89	  Details about disabling write see [HDFS FedBalance](#HDFS_FedBalance).
90	
91	### Command Options
92	
93	Command `submit` has 4 options:
94	
95	| Option key                     | Description                          | Default |
96	| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------ | ------- |
97	| -forceCloseOpen | Force close all open files when there is no diff in the DIFF_DISTCP stage. | Wait until there is no open files. |
98	| -map | Max number of concurrent maps to use for copy. | 10 |
99	| -bandwidth | Specify bandwidth per map in MB. | 10 |
100	| -delay | Specify the delayed duration(millie seconds) when the job needs to retry. | 1000 |
101	| -moveToTrash | This options has 3 values: `trash` (move the source path to trash), `delete` (delete the source path directly) and `skip` (skip both trash and deletion). By default the server side trash interval is used. If the trash is disabled in the server side, the default trash interval 60 minutes is used. | trash |
102	| -diffThreshold | Specify the threshold of the diff entries that used in incremental copy stage. If the diff entries size is no greater than the threshold and the open files check is satisfied(no open files or force close all open files), the fedBalance will go to the final round of distcp. Setting to 0 means waiting until there is no diff.| 0 |
103	
104	### Configuration Options
105	--------------------
106	
107	Set configuration options at hdfs-fedbalance-site.xml.
108	
109	| Configuration key              | Description                          | Default |
110	| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------ | ------- |
111	| hdfs.fedbalance.procedure.work.thread.num | The worker threads number of the BalanceProcedureScheduler. BalanceProcedureScheduler is responsible for scheduling a balance job, including submit, run, delay and recover. | 10 |
112	| hdfs.fedbalance.procedure.scheduler.journal.uri | The uri of the journal, the journal file is used for handling the job persistence and recover. | hdfs://localhost:8020/tmp/procedure |
113	
114	Architecture of HDFS Federation Balance
115	----------------------
116	
117	  The components of the HDFS Federation Balance can be classified into the
118	  following categories:
119	
120	  * Balance Procedure Scheduler
121	  * HDFS FedBalance
122	
123	### Balance Procedure Scheduler
124	
125	  The Balance Procedure Scheduler implements a state machine. It's responsible
126	  for scheduling a balance job, including submit, run, delay and recover.
127	  The model is showed below:
128	
129	  ![Balance Procedure Scheduler](images/BalanceProcedureScheduler.png)
130	
131	  * After a job is submitted, the job is added to the pendingQueue.
132	  * The worker threads take jobs and run them. Journals are written to storage.
133	  * If writing the journal fails, the job is added to the recoverQueue for later
134	    recovery. If Worker thread catches a RetryTaskException, it adds the job to
135	    the delayQueue.
136	  * Rooster thread takes job from delayQueue and adds it back to pendingQueue.
137	  * When a scheduler starts, it scans all the unfinished jobs from the journal
138	    and add them to the recoverQueue. The recover thread will recover them from
139	    the journal and add them back to the pendingQueue.
140	
141	### HDFS FedBalance
142	
143	  HDFS FedBalance is implemented as a job of the state machine. All the distcp
144	  balance logic are implemented here. An HDFS FedBalance job consists of 3
145	  procedures:
146	
147	  * DistCpProcedure: This is the first procedure. It handles all the data copy
148	    works. There are 6 stages:
149	    * PRE_CHECK: Do the pre-check of the src and dst path.
150	    * INIT_DISTCP: Create a snapshot of the source path and distcp it to the
151	      target.
152	    * DIFF_DISTCP: Submit distcp with `-diff` round by round to sync source and
153	      target paths. If `-forceCloseOpen` is set, this stage will finish when
154	      there is no diff between src and dst. Otherwise this stage only finishes
155	      when there is no diff and no open files.
156	    * DISABLE_WRITE: Disable write operations so the src won't be changed. When
157	      working in router mode, it is done by making the mount point readonly.
158	      In normal federation mode it is done by cancelling all the permissions of
159	      the source path.
160	    * FINAL_DISTCP: Force close all the open files and submit the final distcp.
161	    * FINISH: Do the cleanup works. In normal federation mode the finish stage
162	      also restores the permission of the dst path.
163	
164	  * MountTableProcedure: This procedure updates the mount entry in Router. The
165	    readonly is unset and the destination is updated of the mount point. This
166	    procedure is activated only in router based federation mode.
167	
168	  * TrashProcedure: This procedure moves the source path to trash.
169	
170	  After all 3 procedures finish, the balance job is done.
